title: Nuclear size, composition, nuclide notation and isotopes
sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf
paragraphs: An atom has a nucleus. The nucleus is positively charged. The overall dimensions of a nucleus are much smaller than those of an atom. The radius of a nucleus is \(10^{4}\) times smaller than the radius of an atom. This means the volume of a nucleus is about \(10^{12}\) times the smaller than volume of the atom. For an analogy, if an atom is enlarged to the size of a classroom, the nucleus would just be about the size of pinhead. In other words, an atom is almost empty, as (more than 99.9%) of the mass of an atom is concentrated at the nucleus.
Does the nucleus have a structure, just like atoms? Yes there are many similarities between atomic structure and nuclear structure, which makes our study of the properties of the nucleus easier.

In an atom the atomic nucleus is several thousand times more massive than the electrons and occupies only a tiny fraction of the atom’s volume (about 1 part in \(10^{12}\) or less). The nucleus is a bound collection of protons and neutrons. Together, protons and neutrons are referred to as nucleons (particles found inside the nucleus).
In describing the atomic nucleus, we use the following quantities
• The atomic number ‘Z’ (sometimes called the charge number), which is the number of protons in the nucleus.
• The neutron number ‘N’ which is the number of neutrons in the nucleus.
• The mass number ‘A’ which is the number of nucleons in the nucleus (A = Z + N).

In representing nuclei, it is convenient to have a system of symbols to show how many protons and neutrons are present. The symbol used is \({}^{A}_{Z}\mathrm{X}\), where X represents the chemical symbol for the element, Z represents the number of protons and A represents the number of nucleons (i.e number of protons and neutrons) as shown in figure 20.2.

Because the atomic number can also be obtained through the element symbol, therefore we state only the mass number in the superscript and leave out the atomic number subscript, for example \({}^{12}\mathrm{C}\), \({}^{24}\mathrm{Mg}\) and \({}^{35}\mathrm{Cl}\).
The atoms of an element having the same number of protons, or the same atomic number, but having different numbers of neutrons, or different atomic weights is called an isotope.

The binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus is called packing fraction. If ‘A = N + Z’ is the mass number (number of nucleons), then the packing fraction ‘f’ is
The packing fraction (binding fraction) is the measure of stability of a nucleus. The greater the binding energy per nucleon, the more stable the nucleus is.

Since very large repulsive Coulomb forces exists between the close-packed protons in a nucleus, and this force should cause the nucleus to fly apart. Because that does not happen, there must be a counteracting attractive force, this force is called strong nuclear force. The strong nuclear force is a very short range (about 2 fm) attractive force that acts between all nuclear particles. The protons attract each other by means of the nuclear force, and, at the same time, they repel each other through the Coulomb force. The nuclear force also acts between pairs of neutrons and between neutrons and protons. The nuclear force dominates the Coulomb repulsive force within the nucleus (at short ranges), so stable nuclei can exist.

Therefore, the rest energy of the bound system (the nucleus) is less than the combined rest energy of the separated nucleons. To separate the protons and neutron from a nucleus work would need to be done to overcome nuclear force, called binding energy. Binding energy is also equal to the energy liberated when a nucleus is created from other nucleons or nuclei. This nuclear binding energy is derived from the nuclear force and is the energy required to disassemble a nucleus into the same number of free, unbound neutrons and protons it is composed.

paragraphs: Alpha particles are helium nuclei (i.e two protons and two neutrons bound together) emitted from the nucleus. When the ratio of neutrons to protons in the nucleus is too low, certain atoms restore the balance by emitting alpha particles. In alpha decay, the original (parent) nuclide is converted to a ‘daughter’ by the emission of an \(\alpha\) particle. Balancing the reaction shows that the daughter nuclide has a nucleon number reduced by four and a charge reduced by two.

Beta particle emission occurs when the ratio of neutrons to protons in the nucleus is too high. In this case, an excess neutron transforms into a proton and an electron. The proton stays in the nucleus and the electron is ejected energetically. A neutron by itself is unstable; and on average in 890 s will decay into a proton and an electron.
Unlike \(\alpha\)-decay, \(\beta\)-decay of a radionuclide does not change the number of nucleons. In essence, \(\beta\)-decay changes a neutron into a proton.
The emission of a beta particle by thorium-234 results in the formation of protactinium-234
Like beta decay \(\beta^{-}\), positron emission \(\beta^{+}\) does not change the number of nucleons. In essence, \(\beta^{+}\) decay changes a proton into a neutron.

title: Neutrinos, gamma emission and spontaneous random nuclear decay

paragraphs: Notice, in electron emission, an electron antineutrino is also emitted. Whereas the positron emission is accompanied by the emission of an electron neutrino. The electron neutrino is a subatomic particle which has no net electric charge. Like all particles, the electron neutrino has a corresponding antiparticle, the electron antineutrino, which differs only in that some of its properties have equal magnitude but opposite sign.
Why a neutrino is emitted in Beta decay?

Beta decay was a puzzle at first because a continuous spectrum of electron (or positron) kinetic energies was observed. Beta particles are ejected from nucleus at different speeds. In \(\alpha\) decay, the definite kinetic energy is same for all particles to conserve energy and momentum. For the same reasons, scientists thought that \(\beta\) particles emitted in a given decay reaction should also be monoenergetic.

Wolfgang Pauli suggested that not one, but two particles were being emitted in beta decay an electron/positron and neutrino/antineutrino. If a nucleus emits two particles instead of one, then they can conserve both energy and momentum while splitting up the kinetic energy in every possible way. Two momentum vectors that add to zero must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, but three momentum vectors can add to zero in an infinite number of ways and still share the same total kinetic energy. The neutrino has the following properties:
• A mass much smaller than that of the electron, but probably not zero.
• (Recent experiments suggest that the neutrino definitely has mass, but the value is uncertain, perhaps less than \(1\ \mathrm{eV}/c^2\).)
• Very weak interaction with matter, making it difficult to detect

Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation emitted from the nucleus. Gamma radiation emission occurs when the nucleus of a radioactive atom has excess energy. Inside the nucleus the nucleons (like the orbital electrons) exists in discrete-energy states or levels. When a nucleus changes from an excited energy state to a lower energy state, a photon is emitted. The photon has a much greater energy and is called a \(\gamma\) ray. In most cases the \(\alpha\) or \(\beta\) emission from the nucleus leave it in excited state such nuclei achieve further stability by emitting gamma rays.

A process of disintegration that occurs when unstable nuclei decay in an attempt to attain stability is called nuclear decay. This process is both spontaneous and random.

A process without defined pattern, rule or method is called random process. Nuclear decay is unpredictable because precise moment of disintegration is not known for a particular nuclei. Individual disintegrations occur randomly.

A process occurring without apparent external cause is called spontaneous process. Nuclear decay is spontaneous, because the process of radioactive decay cannot be speeded up or slowed down by physical or chemical means.

The time it takes for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay is called half life.
Individual disintegrations are random, however, the probability of decay for nuclei in a sample has fixed value, which is characteristic of that material.

paragraphs: A nuclear reactor is a device that is designed to maintain a self sustaining fission reaction in a controlled manner.

Since large amount of energy is released in a fission process, therefore it is carried under controlled conditions. This energy can be used for useful purposes such as to produce power and radioisotopes. The Nuclear reactor has five main parts as shown in figure 20.18.

The core contain nuclear fuel in which fission is achieved by thermal neutrons, for example, the nuclear fuel may be thin rods about 1 cm in diameter. Uranium \({}^{235}\mathrm{U}\) is a common reactor fuel. Most commercial reactors use uranium in which the amount of \({}^{235}\mathrm{U}\) has been enriched to about 3%.

The material that slows down the neutrons is called a moderator. Neutrons with energies of about 0.025 eV are used in fission of \({}^{235}\mathrm{U}\), the neutrons released during the fission process have greater energies of several MeV. Therefore, a nuclear reactor must contain some type of material that decrease or moderate the speed of neutrons so they can fission additional \({}^{235}\mathrm{U}\) nuclei. The material of moderator should be light and should not absorb neutrons, usually graphite and heavy water are used as moderators.

If the output power from a reactor is to remain constant, only one neutron from each fission event must start a new fission. When each fission leads to one additional fission—no more or no less—the reactor is said to be critical. A reactor normally operates in a critical condition.
Sub-critical and Super-critical state of reactors
What happens when reactor is not operated in critical state?

The reactor is subcritical when, on average, the neutrons from each fission trigger less than one subsequent fission. In a subcritical reactor, the chain reaction is not self-sustaining and eventually stops. When the neutrons from each fission trigger more than one additional fission, the reactor is supercritical. During a supercritical condition, the energy released by a reactor increases. If left unchecked, the increasing energy can lead to a partial or total meltdown of the reactor core.

Therefore, a control mechanism is needed to keep the reactor in its normal, or critical, state. This control is accomplished by a number of control rods that can be moved into and out of the reactor core. The control rods contain an element, such as boron, cadmium or hafnium, that absorbs neutrons. These control rods are moved in and out of reactor core to keep reactor in critical state.

The coolant is used to cool the fuel rods and the moderator, and is capable of carrying away heat generated in fission process. Without Heat exchange system the core assembly can melt under enormous heat. The heat generated within the fuel rods is carried away by water that surrounds the rods. The hot water is pumped through a heat exchanger, where heat is transferred to water flowing in a second, closed system.

paragraphs: One of the most important applications of nuclear physics has been in medicine, for both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.

Radioactive isotopes are used in medical diagnosis as tracers. Radioactive isotopes are introduced in the body in chemical forms that have an affinity for certain organs, such as bone or the thyroid gland. For medical diagnosis, the radionuclide commonly used today is \({}^{99\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{Tc}\) long-lived excited state of technetium-99 (the “m” in the symbol stands for ‘metastable’ state).

A sensitive detector (called a “gamma-ray camera”) can observe the radiations from the isotopes that are concentrated in the organ and can produce an image that shows how the activity is distributed in the patient. These detectors are capable of determining where each gamma-ray photon originates in the patient as shown in figure 20.24.

Another technique that reveals information inside the body is positron emission tomography (PET), in which the patient is injected with a positron-emitting isotope that is readily absorbed by the body. Examples of isotopes used are \({}^{15}\mathrm{O}\) (\(t_{1/2}=2\ \mathrm{min}\)), \({}^{13}\mathrm{N}\) (\(t_{1/2}=10\ \mathrm{min}\)), \({}^{11}\mathrm{C}\) (\(t_{1/2}=20\ \mathrm{min}\)), and \({}^{18}\mathrm{F}\) (\(t_{1/2}=110\ \mathrm{min}\)). These isotopes are produced with a cyclotron. By surrounding the patient with a ring of detectors, it is possible to determine exactly where the decay occurred, and from a large number of such events, an image is produced that reconstructs the distribution of the radioisotope in the patient.

All particles in nature are subjected to four fundamental forces, strong force, weak force, electromagnetic force and gravitational force.

The strong force is very short range about \(10^{-14}\ \mathrm{m}\) and is responsible for binding of nucleons in the nucleus. It can be considered as an exchange force in which the exchange particles are gluon. It is the strongest of all the forces and have been assigned as relative strength 1.

Fundamentally, both magnetic and electric forces are manifestations of an exchange force involving the exchange of photons. The electromagnetic force holds atoms and molecules together. It has infinite range and relative strength is \(10^{-2}\).

Weak interaction involves the exchange of the intermediate vector bosons, the W and the Z. The weak interaction changes one flavor of quark into another. It is very short range about 0.1% of diameter of proton i.e \(10^{-18}\ \mathrm{m}\). It have relative strength of about \(10^{-6}\).

paragraphs: Gravity is long range force and is the weakest of the four fundamental forces having relative strength of \(10^{-43}\), yet it is the dominant force in the universe for shaping the large scale structure of galaxies, stars, etc. Viewed as an exchange force, the massless exchange particle is called the graviton (however it is not confirmed yet).
Force — Particle acted on by force — Relative strength — Typical Lifetimes for decay via given interaction (s) — Force carrying exchange particle

Beginning in about 1945, many new particles were discovered in experiments involving high-energy collisions between known particles. Such particles are highly unstable and have very short half-lives, ranging between \(10^{6}\) and \(10^{23}\ \mathrm{s}\). So far, more than 400 of these unstable, temporary particles have been catalogued.
It is useful to group the known particles into three families—the bosons, the leptons, and the hadrons.

The boson family is composed of particles that play central roles in nature’s fundamental forces. The photon is associated with the electromagnetic force. The \(\mathrm{W}^{-}\), \(\mathrm{W}^{+}\), and \(\mathrm{Z}^{0}\) particles are associated with the weak nuclear force. The gluons are associated with the strong nuclear force, whereas the graviton is thought to be associated with the gravitational force.

The lepton family consists of particles that interact by means of the weak nuclear force. Leptons can also exert gravitational and (if the leptons are charged) electromagnetic forces on other particles. The four better-known leptons are the electron, the muon, the electron neutrino \(
u_{e}\), and the muon neutrino \(
u_{\mu}\). Two other leptons have also been discovered, the tau particle \(	au\) and its neutrino \(
u_{	au}\), bringing the number of particles in the lepton family to six. No internal structure for leptons is observed so far, therefore they are considered to be elementary.

The hadron family contains the particles that interact by means of both the strong nuclear force and the weak nuclear force. Hadrons can also interact by gravitational and electromagnetic forces, but at short distances the strong nuclear force dominates. Among the hadrons are the proton, the neutron, and the pions. The hadrons are subdivided into two groups, the mesons and the baryons.

paragraphs: As more and more hadrons were discovered, it became clear that they were not all elementary particles. The suggestion was made that the hadrons are made up of smaller, more elementary particles called quarks. In-1963, a quark theory was initiated independently by M. Gell-Mann (1929- ) and G. Zweig (1937- ).
Quark Model is based on the following assumptions:
1. There are six types of quark up (u), down (d), strange (s), charm (c), top (t) and bottom (b).
2. Every quark has corresponding antiquark denoted by the same letter with a bar over it.
According to the original quark model of hadrons, all mesons consist of a quark and an antiquark, whereas baryons contain three quarks.

3. Quarks combine in three to form baryons (proton, neutron, sigma e.t.c.) and antiquarks combine in three to form anti-baryons (anti-proton, anti-neutron, anti-sigma e.t.c.) as shown in figure 20.27.
4. Quarks combine with antiquarks in twos to form mesons.

Electric charge comes in only one kind (positive) and its opposite (negative), but strong charge comes in three kinds (called red, blue, and green), each of which has an opposite (called antired, antiblue, and antigreen). Color charge has nothing to do with the colors of light that we perceive visually. They are based on an analogy: just as the red, blue, and green dots produced by different phosphors on a TV screen combine to make white, a red quark, blue quark, and green quark combine to form a colorless (white) combination.

All free particles have a color charge of zero. A baryon always contains one quark of each color, an antibaryon always contains one antiquark of each anticolor, and a meson always contains a quark of one color and an antiquark of the corresponding anticolor, such as a red quark and an antired antiquark. In each case, the strong force holds quarks together in colorless combinations, similar to the way the electromagnetic force holds negative and positive charges together to form a neutral atom with zero net electric charge.
